nodes.norm_label: register a sip line (advanced event-driven flow)

nodes.label: Architecture Gates (ENGINEERING_RULES)
nodes.rationale: CI enforces ENGINEERING_RULES architecture constraints via a dedicated ArchitectureTests project as a gate before the general test+coverage run, on both ubuntu and windows matrix legs.

nodes.label: Documentation Build Workflow
nodes.rationale: Builds Core and Client API projects first to generate XML docs, then builds the DocFX site as a PR/push validation artifact (7-day retention), without deploying.

nodes.label: NuGet Packages Workflow
nodes.rationale: Publishing goes to nuget.org via NUGET_API_KEY (not GITHUB_TOKEN), so contents:read permission is enough. Version resolves from workflow_dispatch input or the v* tag name.

nodes.label: Release Documentation Workflow
nodes.rationale: Injects the release tag version into DocFX globalMetadata via jq and publishes both a root copy and a version-pinned copy of the site to GitHub Pages.

nodes.label: Symmetric RTP (Comedia) NAT Traversal
nodes.rationale: Chosen so inbound media over a public SIP trunk behind NAT flows without STUN or ICE; combined with a NAT-public contact learned from the registrar's received=/rport= (RFC 3261 s18.2.1 / RFC 3581) and trunk-DID line matching. Verified end-to-end by a real call and packet capture.

nodes.label: Record-Route Echo Fix (RFC 3261 s12.1.1)
nodes.rationale: Responses previously omitted the request's Record-Route headers, leaving the peer's route set empty; ACK/BYE then went straight to our Contact from an un-primed far-end node, which restricted NATs drop — the confirmed root cause of ACK/BYE never arriving over the trunk.

nodes.label: Media-Inactivity Timeout
nodes.rationale: A connected call whose inbound RTP goes silent is torn down as a NAT-safe fallback for a far-end BYE that never reaches the in-dialog Contact. Configurable via SdkConfiguration.InboundMediaTimeout (0 disables).

nodes.label: Module Registry (IVoipClientModule)
nodes.rationale: Generic extension point so feature modules ship as separate packages (DI before AddCallora or client.Modules.Register). Replaced unimplemented module facades that threw ModuleFeatureUnavailableException on every call; those capabilities return as separate plugin packages built on the public media API. Modules become resolvable only after OnAttached completes.

nodes.label: Per-Call Media Tap Contract
nodes.rationale: Pinned as a public, tested contract: parallel IMediaReceiver fan-out, detach/dispose isolation, IMediaSender injection, format discovery via ICall.MediaParameters. FrameReceived runs synchronously on the media path; consumers must buffer.

nodes.label: PreferredAudioCodecs Codec Preference
nodes.rationale: Ordered audio codec preference by SDP encoding name drives offers, answers and the primary codec of RTP sessions consistently; unsupported names are ignored, no match falls back to SDK defaults. Driven by G.711 u-law passthrough interop with an AVM Fritz!Box AI-agent scenario.

nodes.label: RFC 3550 Jitter Estimator Fix
nodes.rationale: Arrival-time conversion to RTP units saturated on a double-to-uint overflow, so reported jitter converged to the 20 ms frame interval on a clean link instead of ~0; now computed in integer math truncated modulo 2^32. RTT from RTCP receiver reports (LSR/DLSR) now feeds the adaptive jitter buffer instead of reporting the static 60 ms default.

nodes.label: VoipClient Public Facade
nodes.rationale: VoipClient is the central, supported integration surface; Infrastructure types are internal implementation details and Application types are only exposed where necessary — keeps the external API compact and stable while allowing internal evolution.

nodes.label: CalloraVoipSdk.Audio.Windows Package
nodes.rationale: Windows audio integration based on NAudio.

nodes.label: CalloraVoipSdk.Audio.Linux Package
nodes.rationale: Linux audio integration based on PortAudio.

nodes.label: Module Registry (client.Modules)
nodes.rationale: Extension point for feature modules shipped as separate packages: implement IVoipClientModule, attach, resolve by any implemented interface via Get<T>/TryGet<T>.

nodes.label: Per-Call Media Tap
nodes.rationale: IMediaReceiver.FrameReceived fires synchronously on the media path — handlers must buffer and return immediately, never block. Negotiated format available via ICall.MediaParameters.

nodes.label: DDD-Oriented Architecture
nodes.rationale: Domain (entities, value objects, states, domain events), Application (use cases, orchestration), Infrastructure (SIP/RTP/SDP/audio implementations), Client (facade, convenience APIs, DI) — clear boundaries so infrastructure stays a non-public integration surface.

nodes.label: Commercial Plugin Line-up (Callora.Realtime/WebSocket/Privacy/Risk/Intelligence)
nodes.rationale: SDK core stays open and free; advanced capabilities ship as paid plugins on a private feed (not nuget.org), licensed separately — e.g. Callora.Realtime bridges call audio to realtime AI APIs with pacing, backpressure and barge-in.

nodes.label: Call State Machine
nodes.rationale: Outbound: Dialing -> Ringing -> Connected <-> OnHold -> Terminated; inbound: Ringing -> Accept/Reject/Redirect. State changes are always delivered on a background thread; wrong-state actions throw InvalidOperationException; after Terminated the ICall object is inert and must not be reused.

nodes.label: RTP Receive Path
nodes.rationale: Network -> UDP -> RTP Receiver -> demux -> Jitter Buffer -> PCM Decode -> IMediaReceiver.

nodes.label: RTP Send Path
nodes.rationale: IMediaSender -> PCM Encode -> RTP Packetize -> SRTP Encrypt -> UDP -> Network.

nodes.label: Demo App Walkthrough
nodes.rationale: Interactive console app demonstrating the full call lifecycle against a real SIP server: registration via ConnectAsync, default audio attach on Connected, keyboard call control, busy-reject of concurrent inbound calls, graceful cleanup.

nodes.label: Getting Started Guide
nodes.rationale: Both a convenience flow (ConnectAsync) and an advanced event-driven flow (client.Lines.Register + StateChanged) are supported; convenience is additive, the low-level flow remains unchanged.

nodes.label: Per-Call Media Tap (Guide)
nodes.rationale: CreateReceiver/CreateSender give raw frame access to any call — foundation for voice bots, AI bridging and custom streaming. FrameReceived fires synchronously on the media path; buffer into e.g. a Channel<T> and return immediately.

nodes.label: Recording & Playback (WAV/MP3)
nodes.rationale: WAV end-to-end; MP3 via ffmpeg-backed infrastructure adapter; MP3-negotiated calls use passthrough without re-encoding. Optional encryption via RecordingOptions.EncryptionProvider (e.g. AesGcmRecordingEncryptionProvider). Built-in payload transcoding covers L16/PCMU/PCMA/G.722. Conference variants require an IMixedMediaBus — since 2.0.0 the core ships no conferencing; the mix bus comes from own wiring or the future commercial conferencing plugin.

nodes.label: Commercial Plugins (Callora.*)
nodes.rationale: SDK core is open and free; advanced capabilities (Realtime, WebSocket, Privacy, Risk, Intelligence) ship as paid plugins on a private feed, built on the public module registry and media-tap contract.

nodes.label: Sovereign Telephony Core
nodes.rationale: European B2B voice runtime positioning: full protocol stack (SIP, RTP, SRTP, SDP, STUN) owned in-house, no vendor lock-in — full technical control over telephony, media path and decision logic.

nodes.label: DocFX API Filter Rules
nodes.rationale: Excludes ObsoleteAttribute members and the CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Infrastructure and CalloraVoipSdk.Core.Application.Ports namespaces/types from generated API docs — the published reference mirrors the supported public API boundary.
